latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Sustained antigenic load from infection (EBV/CMV/leishmania/HIV), malignancy (especially T/NK lymphoma), or active rheumatologic disease (sJIA, AOSD, SLE) that drives the hyperinflammatory loop.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Impaired NK/CTL cytotoxic clearance of antigen-presenting cells
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Genetic (PRF1, UNC13D, STX11, STXBP2, RAB27A, XIAP, SAP) or acquired loss of perforin/granule-mediated killing prevents elimination of stimulated APCs and infected cells, allowing prolonged T cell–macrophage cross-stimulation. Core upstream lesion of HLH.
Hypersecretion of IFN-γ by activated CD8 T and NK cells; central effector cytokine driving macrophage activation, hemophagocytosis, and tissue injury. CXCL9 is its serum surrogate.
IFN-γ–driven activation of tissue macrophages with hypersecretion of ferritin, sCD25, TNF, IL-6, IL-18, plasminogen activator, and engulfment of hematopoietic cells in BM/spleen/LN/liver.

NLRP3-mediated IL-1β/IL-18 release from activated macrophages, especially prominent in MAS (sJIA/AOSD-related); marked IL-18 elevation distinguishes MAS from primary HLH and predicts anakinra responsiveness.
Macrophage- and T-cell–derived IL-6 drives CRP, fibrinogen synthesis (often masked by macrophage plasminogen activator–induced fibrinogen consumption), fever, and hepcidin response.

Activated lymphocyte/macrophage infiltration of liver sinusoids, spleen, and BM producing transaminitis, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, hypoalbuminemia, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and fulminant-hepatitis-like presentations.

Macrophage-secreted plasminogen activator and tissue factor cause hypofibrinogenemia, elevated D-dimer, prolonged PT/aPTT, DIC-like picture; distinct from septic DIC by very high ferritin and falling fibrinogen with relatively preserved platelet count early.
Suppression of hematopoiesis (IFN-γ, TNF) plus active macrophage engulfment of erythrocytes, platelets, granulocytes producing bi/tri-lineage cytopenia; not primarily peripheral immune destruction.

Magnitude of EBV/CMV/HIV/leishmania/other pathogen replication when HLH is infection-triggered; persistence sustains the cytokine storm and predicts treatment failure without trigger-directed therapy.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Subclinical pre-MAS pressure in active rheumatologic disease
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Smoldering inflammasome and IFN-γ-axis priming during sJIA/AOSD/SLE flares prior to overt MAS; ferritin trend, glycosylated ferritin fraction, and IL-18 capture this pressure.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Genetic predisposition unmasks impaired clearance under heavy antigen load; acquired triggers also exhaust CTL/NK function.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Antigenic stimulation in a host with reduced perforin/granule cytotoxicity produces sustained APC stimulation rather than clearance.
Persistent APC–T cell synapse leads to CD8/NK hypersecretion of IFN-γ, the central HLH effector cytokine.
IFN-γ is the principal activator of tissue macrophages driving hemophagocytosis and downstream cytokine release.
Activated macrophages assemble NLRP3 and release IL-1β/IL-18, amplifying the loop and recruiting further T-cell IFN-γ.
IL-18 is a potent inducer of IFN-γ in NK and Th1 cells, closing a positive feedback loop characteristic of MAS.
Activated macrophages secrete IL-6 driving CRP, hepcidin, and acute phase response.
Activated macrophages and hepatocytes secrete ferritin in massive quantities; ferritin >10,000 ng/mL is highly specific for HLH.
Activated T cells shed soluble CD25; sIL-2R is a HLH-2004 criterion and tracks T-cell activation.
CXCL9 is an IFN-γ–induced chemokine; serum CXCL9 is a high-fidelity surrogate of active IFN-γ signaling and tracks treatment response.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Sensitivity is moderate (~60%); absence does not exclude HLH.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Direct morphologic evidence of macrophage engulfment of hematopoietic cells, supportive HLH-2004 criterion.
Macrophage hemophagocytosis plus IFN-γ/TNF marrow suppression produce bi/tri-lineage cytopenia.
Erythrophagocytosis and suppressed erythropoiesis drop hemoglobin, often <9 g/dL (HLH-2004).
Falling platelets <100×10⁹/L is an early and sensitive MAS sign in sJIA/AOSD even before overt cytopenia.
Suppressed granulopoiesis drives ANC <1.0×10⁹/L (HLH-2004 criterion).

mechanism_edges.conditionality: In sJIA/AOSD baseline leukocytosis, MAS may produce relative drop without true leukopenia.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Paradoxical fall of WBC during a flare of underlying autoinflammatory disease is a key MAS clue.
Macrophage-secreted plasminogen activator and tissue factor produce hyperfibrinolytic + consumptive coagulopathy.
Hypofibrinogenemia (<150 mg/dL) is HLH-2004 criterion; falling fibrinogen during sJIA flare is a sentinel MAS marker.
Hyperfibrinolysis from macrophage-derived plasminogen activator markedly elevates D-dimer.
Combined hepatic synthetic dysfunction and consumption prolong PT/INR.
Factor consumption and hepatic dysfunction prolong aPTT.
Severe HLH coagulopathy meets ISTH DIC criteria and predicts hemorrhagic complications.
Hepatic and splenic infiltration by activated lymphocytes and macrophages causes organomegaly and hepatocellular injury.
Lymphohistiocytic hepatitis raises ALT, often 3–20× ULN.
AST often higher than ALT in fulminant HLH hepatitis; severe rises portend fulminant phenotype.
Tissue injury and hemophagocytosis raise LDH, often >1000 U/L; pattern overlaps with TMA but with much higher ferritin.
Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia from cholestatic hepatitis pattern; prognostic marker.
Hepatic synthetic dysfunction and capillary leak lower albumin.
Splenic histiocytic infiltration produces palpable splenomegaly, an HLH-2004 criterion.
Lymphohistiocytic hepatitis with hepatomegaly common in MAS and HLH.
Severe HLH may present as ALF; high AST/ALT, INR, and ammonia indicate liver failure trajectory.
TNF-α suppresses lipoprotein lipase causing hypertriglyceridemia ≥265 mg/dL (HLH-2004 criterion).
IL-6 drives hepatic CRP; CRP markedly elevated but often disproportionately lower than ferritin in HLH/MAS.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Falling ESR in active sJIA flare, due to hypofibrinogenemia.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Paradoxical fall of ESR (despite high CRP) is a classical sJIA-MAS clue, reflecting fibrinogen consumption.
Sustained high fever (often >38.5°C, often persistent or biphasic) is a near-universal HLH-2004 criterion.
IFN-γ and IL-18 act centrally to raise temperature; HLH fever may be antibiotic-refractory.
Marked IL-6 elevation; pattern overlaps with sepsis but coexists with very high ferritin and IL-18 in HLH/MAS.
Reduced or absent NK cytotoxicity (HLH-2004 criterion); persistent absence after treatment suggests primary HLH.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More prominent in EBV-HLH and lymphoma-associated HLH.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Reactive or neoplastic lymphadenopathy frequent in EBV-HLH and lymphoma-driven HLH; biopsy may be diagnostic.
CNS infiltration causes seizures, encephalopathy, ataxia, focal deficits; ~30–40% of HLH and high mortality marker.
Encephalopathy from cytokine storm and CNS lymphohistiocytic infiltration.
Seizures occur in CNS-HLH; intrathecal MTX/steroids indicated when CSF abnormal or imaging positive.
Glycosylated ferritin <20% is highly specific for AOSD/MAS, distinguishing from other hyperferritinemic states.
Active macrophage activation defines the syndrome and drives transition to overt MAS in rheumatologic disease.
Untreated HLH mortality ≥50%; persistent high macrophage activation despite therapy is the principal driver of death.
Coagulopathy with bleeding, including DAH and ICH, is a major proximate cause of death.
Liver failure with INR rise, hyperbilirubinemia, and encephalopathy indicates terminal trajectory without rescue therapy.
CNS-HLH carries higher mortality and long-term neurologic morbidity.
Active pathogen replication is the antigenic source in infection-triggered HLH.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV-HLH; high EBV PCR predicts response to rituximab and need for etoposide.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: EBV viremia (often >10⁴ copies/mL) sustains B-cell antigenic load driving CTL activation.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: sJIA/AOSD/SLE flares with rising ferritin and falling fibrinogen.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pre-MAS rheumatologic activity transitions to overt MAS when feedback loop saturates.
The disease can present with persistent or recurrent fever over the observed clinical history.
HLH/MAS fever may persist despite antibacterial therapy unless the trigger and immune activation are controlled.
Pulmonary, cardiac, serosal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement can cause dyspnea.
Pulmonary or airway involvement can cause cough.
Cytokine storm, CNS involvement, shock, and metabolic derangement can cause encephalopathy in severe HLH/MAS.

axes.shape_free_text: Persistent or biphasic high fever, often >38.5°C, frequently antibiotic-refractory; HLH-2004 criterion threshold ≥38.5°C ≥7 days.
Sinus tachycardia tracking fever and cytokine storm; can be marked in shock-like phenotypes.
Tachypnea from cytokine storm, ALI/ARDS, or compensatory metabolic acidosis.
Often preserved early; falls in cytokine-storm shock and MOF; vasopressor-requiring phenotype carries high mortality.
Usually preserved; falls with ARDS, DAH, or pulmonary HLH/MAS infiltration.
Hallmark marker; HLH-2004 threshold ≥500 ng/mL but typical HLH/MAS values 5,000–100,000+; ferritin >10,000 has ~90% specificity for HLH in pediatrics; trend tracks treatment response.
Markedly decreased (<0.20) in AOSD-MAS and HLH; useful to discriminate from other hyperferritinemic states such as iron overload or simple infection.
HLH-2004 threshold ≥2400 U/mL; very high values (≥10,000) suggest lymphoma-associated HLH; marker of T-cell activation.
IFN-γ surrogate; markedly elevated in active HLH/MAS; used as a pharmacodynamic biomarker for emapalumab and ruxolitinib response.
Decreased or absent in HLH; persistent absence post-recovery suggests primary HLH and triggers genetic testing for PRF1, UNC13D, STX11, STXBP2, RAB27A.
Histologic engulfment of erythrocytes/platelets/granulocytes by macrophages in BM, spleen, LN, or liver; sensitivity ~60%, may be missed early or in patchy disease.
Anemia (typically <9 g/dL per HLH-2004) from hemophagocytosis and marrow suppression; non-immune (DAT often negative).
HLH-2004 threshold <100×10⁹/L; in MAS, falling platelets during a sJIA flare are a sensitive early sign even before crossing threshold.
HLH-2004 threshold <1.0×10⁹/L; deepens with etoposide and disease progression.
Often falls; in sJIA/AOSD baseline leukocytosis a paradoxical drop is the key MAS clue.
HLH-2004 threshold ≤150 mg/dL; falling fibrinogen during sJIA flare (despite high CRP and inflammation) is a sentinel MAS marker; due to macrophage plasminogen activator.
HLH-2004 threshold ≥265 mg/dL fasting; due to TNF-α–mediated lipoprotein lipase suppression.
Transaminitis from lymphohistiocytic hepatitis; 3–20× ULN typical; may rise to thousands in fulminant phenotype.
Often higher than ALT in HLH; also reflects hemolysis and tissue injury.
Marked elevation from tissue injury, hemophagocytosis, and lymphoma trigger if present; values >1000 common.
Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia from cholestatic hepatitis; >5 mg/dL marks severe hepatic involvement.
Falls due to capillary leak and hepatic dysfunction; prognostic.
Markedly elevated reflecting hyperfibrinolysis; tracks coagulopathy severity.
Prolonged in severe HLH from hepatic synthetic dysfunction and consumption; INR >1.5 marks high mortality risk.
Prolonged from factor consumption and hepatic dysfunction.
Markedly elevated; ratio of ferritin to CRP often disproportionately high in HLH/MAS compared with bacterial sepsis.
Paradoxical fall during MAS in active sJIA flare due to fibrinogen consumption; classical clue.
Often only mildly elevated in pure HLH/MAS unless concurrent bacterial sepsis; helps differentiate sepsis from HLH/MAS but is imperfect.
Markedly elevated; pattern overlaps sepsis but coexists with very high ferritin and IL-18.
Rises with cytokine-storm AKI, hypoperfusion, or rhabdomyolysis-like picture; predicts mortality.
Elevated in severe MOF/shock; ≥4 mmol/L marks high-risk phenotype.
Palpable splenomegaly in majority; HLH-2004 criterion.
Common; tracks hepatic infiltration.
Particularly prominent in EBV-HLH and lymphoma-associated HLH; biopsy may be diagnostic for trigger.
From thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy; mucosal bleeding heralds severe DIC.
Salmon-pink evanescent rash in AOSD/sJIA-MAS; persistent fixed rash in some HLH variants.
CNS HLH/MAS or severe systemic inflammation can produce encephalopathy or altered mental status.
Seizures in CNS-HLH; require LP, MRI, intrathecal therapy when CSF abnormal.
EBV-driven HLH common in adolescents/adults from East Asia; high load >10⁴–10⁶ predicts need for rituximab; tracks treatment response.
CMV-triggered HLH especially post-HSCT or in HIV/immunocompromised.
Probability that the syndrome is HLH/MAS based on HLH-2004 (≥5/8 criteria), HScore (>169 ~85% probability), MAS-2016 criteria for sJIA, and exclusion of mimics; gates etoposide and emapalumab use.
Probability of underlying T/NK or B-cell lymphoma (especially EBV-driven NK/T) driving HLH; in adults >40, lymphoma is the leading trigger; sIL-2R/ferritin ratio >2 raises suspicion.
Probability of an active infectious trigger (EBV, CMV, leishmania, HIV, dengue, etc.) requiring concurrent pathogen-directed therapy.
Probability that the syndrome is MAS complicating sJIA/AOSD/SLE/Kawasaki; gates anakinra/cyclosporine over etoposide.
Captures marrow reserve and dose-modification needs (renal, hepatic, prior chemo) for etoposide.
Hyperbilirubinemia or INR rise mandating etoposide dose reduction (50% if bilirubin 1.5–3 mg/dL; consider hold >3 mg/dL).
Requires dose adjustment of etoposide and methotrexate; cyclosporine nephrotoxicity concern.
Captures cumulative immunosuppression burden from steroids + etoposide ± cyclosporine ± JAKi; drives prophylaxis.
Rituximab + steroids high HBV reactivation risk; mandates HBsAg/anti-HBc screening and entecavir prophylaxis when indicated.
Severe HLH coagulopathy plus pulmonary inflammation can precipitate DAH; high mortality.
Coagulopathy + thrombocytopenia + CNS-HLH increase ICH risk.
30–40% of HLH/MAS develops CNS involvement; high mortality and long-term morbidity; LP/MRI mandatory if any neurologic sign.
ALF phenotype with very high AST/ALT, INR, and encephalopathy; portends high mortality without rescue therapy and possibly LT.
Coagulopathy meeting ISTH DIC criteria common in severe HLH; bleeding more typical than thrombosis.
Cytokine-storm ARDS, DAH, or pulmonary HLH/MAS infiltration drive respiratory failure.
Steroid + etoposide + cytopenia drive bacterial, fungal, viral reactivation infections; PJP, Aspergillus, candidemia, CMV, HSV.
Daily hazard of progression to overt MAS/HLH from a smoldering pre-MAS state in active rheumatologic disease.
Untreated HLH mortality ≥50%; treated 30–50% in adults, ~20–30% in pediatrics; lymphoma-associated and CNS-HLH worst.
History-level fever burden over days to months, distinct from a single measured body temperature.

axes.display_name: Lack of clinical response to standard antibacterial therapy
axes.shape_free_text: Persistent fever, inflammation, or organ findings despite antibacterial therapy that should have covered ordinary bacterial infection.
Patient-reported or observed breathlessness from pulmonary, cardiac, mediastinal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement.
Dry or productive cough as a symptom axis; mechanism depends on pulmonary, airway, cardiac, or mediastinal involvement.
Trigger-context axis for dermatomyositis or inflammatory myopathy associated HLH/MAS; not a core HLH mechanism.
Trigger-context axis for dermatomyositis-associated HLH/MAS; not a core HLH mechanism.
Rheumatic trigger/context activity that may accompany MAS/HLH presentations.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Both rise with macrophage activation; co-elevation strengthens HLH probability against simple sepsis.
As macrophage activation rises, ferritin spikes and fibrinogen falls (paradoxically vs typical acute phase response).
Falling fibrinogen drives ESR drop in MAS, the classical paradox in active sJIA flare.
IFN-γ signaling (CXCL9) drives macrophage activation that secretes ferritin; CXCL9 typically tracks slightly ahead of ferritin.
Both fall together as MAS progresses; combined fall is a sensitive sentinel in sJIA flare.
Multilineage cytopenia from hemophagocytosis links platelet and Hb drops.
Hepatocellular injury raises both, with AST often higher in HLH.
Severe transaminitis precedes synthetic dysfunction with INR rise as ALF develops.
Higher diagnostic confidence enables earlier targeted therapy (etoposide, emapalumab, anakinra), reducing mortality.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HLH-94/2004 backbone; high doses (10 mg/m²/day) suppress T-cell activation and macrophage cytokine release.
Concurrent untreated infection worsens; pair with pathogen-directed therapy and empirical antimicrobials.

failure_modes: incomplete cytokine storm suppression in IFN-γ–driven HLH

side_effects.interpretation: demargination leukocytosis can confound MAS WBC trend

treatments.context_specific_role: Backbone of HLH-94/2004 and MAS regimens; first agent in stable MAS prior to escalation; pulse methylprednisolone 30 mg/kg/day for severe MAS.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HLH-94/2004 cornerstone; particularly effective in EBV-HLH by depleting activated T cells.
EBV-HLH is etoposide-sensitive; early etoposide (within 4 weeks) substantially improves survival.
Bilirubin 1.5–3 mg/dL → 50% dose; >3 mg/dL → consider hold; balanced against need to control HLH.
CrCl-based dose reduction needed.
In MAS from sJIA/AOSD, anakinra-based strategies are preferred first-line; etoposide reserved for refractory/severe.

failure_modes: fails when underlying lymphoma drives HLH without lymphoma-directed therapy
treatments.context_specific_role: HLH-94/2004 protocol component; 150 mg/m² twice weekly induction. Early administration in EBV-HLH improves survival. Adult dosing modulated by performance status, organ function.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: First-line for MAS in sJIA/AOSD; rapid response often within hours; safe even with concurrent infection.
MAS with very high IL-18 typically anakinra-responsive.
Anakinra has favorable safety profile in concurrent infection vs broader immunosuppression.

failure_modes: incomplete response in IFN-γ–dominant primary HLH (lower IL-18)
treatments.context_specific_role: First-line for MAS in sJIA/AOSD/SLE; high-dose IV (5–10 mg/kg/day, sometimes higher) used in critically ill MAS; bridge while etiology is clarified.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: FDA-approved for primary HLH refractory/intolerant/recurrent on conventional therapy; targets central IFN-γ axis.
High CXCL9 confirms active IFN-γ signaling and predicts response; serial CXCL9 monitors pharmacodynamics.
IFN-γ blockade increases mycobacterial, fungal, and herpesvirus risk; screen and prophylax.

failure_modes: severe atypical infections (TB, NTM, fungal, HSV/VZV)
treatments.context_specific_role: Primary/refractory HLH bridge to HSCT; emerging use in MAS with very high CXCL9.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: JAK1/2 inhibition blocks IFN-γ, IL-6, GM-CSF signaling; effective in salvage/refractory secondary HLH.

treatments.context_specific_role: Salvage in steroid-refractory MAS/HLH; emerging first-line option in some adult sHLH protocols.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Effective in MAS from sJIA/AOSD; steroid-sparing maintenance after acute control.
Nephrotoxicity, hypertension, PRES; avoid in severe renal injury.

failure_modes: PRES (posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome) – major in MAS due to TMA-prone state

side_effects.interpretation: PRES risk, especially in active MAS

treatments.context_specific_role: HLH-94/2004 maintenance; second-line for MAS after anakinra/steroids; useful for steroid-sparing once acute phase controlled.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Useful adjunct in infection-triggered HLH (especially when no specific antiviral exists) and in suspected autoimmune contributions.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunct, particularly in infection-triggered HLH and pediatric MAS; not curative.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: EBV-HLH driven by infected B cells; rituximab depletes B cell reservoir, lowers EBV load.
Component of lymphoma-directed therapy in B-NHL–associated HLH.
HBV reactivation can be fatal; mandatory screening and prophylaxis if HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+.

failure_modes: hypogammaglobulinemia and prolonged B-cell depletion infections
treatments.context_specific_role: Pair with etoposide-based regimens in EBV-HLH (CD20+) and B-cell lymphoma–associated HLH.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Indicated when CSF abnormal (pleocytosis, elevated protein) or MRI shows HLH lesions; HLH-2004 protocol for CNS-HLH.
LP risk with severe coagulopathy/thrombocytopenia; correct before procedure.

failure_modes: incomplete CNS control if systemic disease unaddressed
treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunct to systemic therapy when CNS-HLH documented.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Curative for primary/familial HLH and refractory secondary HLH; reduced-intensity conditioning preferred.

treatments.context_specific_role: Curative therapy for primary HLH and select refractory/relapsed secondary HLH; bridge with emapalumab/etoposide.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Bridge to HSCT in refractory HLH; depletes T and B cells via CD52.

failure_modes: severe opportunistic infections (CMV reactivation, fungal, PJP)
treatments.context_specific_role: Salvage option as bridge to HSCT in refractory HLH.

biallelic_PRF1_UNC13D_STX11_STXBP2.trajectory_modulation: Earlier onset (often infancy/childhood), more severe, refractory to non-HSCT therapy; absent NK cytotoxicity persists post-treatment.

XLP_SH2D1A_XIAP.trajectory_modulation: EBV-triggered fulminant HLH in males; XIAP HLH often less severe but recurrent and difficult to transplant.

RAB27A_LYST_AP3B1_syndromic.trajectory_modulation: Griscelli/Chediak-Higashi/HPS2 syndromic HLH with characteristic skin/hair features.

high_load_active_replication.trajectory_modulation: Most common infectious trigger globally, especially in East Asian populations; T/NK-cell EBV-HLH carries worst prognosis.

T_NK_cell_lymphoma.trajectory_modulation: Adult HLH leading trigger; very high sIL-2R/ferritin ratio; lymphoma-directed therapy required for cure.

leukemia_acute.trajectory_modulation: HLH at diagnosis or during induction chemotherapy.

sjia_active_flare.trajectory_modulation: Lifetime MAS risk ~10–15%; sentinel signs are paradoxical fall of platelets, fibrinogen, ESR with rising ferritin and AST.

aosd_active_flare.trajectory_modulation: Glycosylated ferritin <20% strongly supportive; anakinra responsive.

sle_active_flare.trajectory_modulation: Lupus-MAS overlap: ferritin trend and CXCL9 help distinguish from active SLE flare alone.

kawasaki_disease.trajectory_modulation: Rare MAS variant; resistant to IVIG.

post_hsct_or_solid_organ_transplant.trajectory_modulation: CMV/EBV/HHV6-driven HLH common; differential vs. GVHD challenging.

hiv_advanced.trajectory_modulation: Multiple co-infections (CMV, leishmania, mycobacteria, lymphoma); HLH may unmask AIDS.

checkpoint_inhibitor_or_car_t_therapy.trajectory_modulation: Immune-related HLH/CRS overlap; tocilizumab and steroids first-line in CAR-T HLH.

visceral_leishmaniasis_exposure.trajectory_modulation: Treatable cause; antileishmanial therapy curative; consider in travelers/Mediterranean/African/South American/South Asian patients.

tuberculosis_disseminated.trajectory_modulation: Treat TB before/with HLH-directed therapy; cytokine storm mimic and trigger.

infant_under_1_year.trajectory_modulation: Higher prior probability of primary HLH; strongly consider genetic testing and HSCT.

child_or_adolescent.trajectory_modulation: Mixed primary/secondary; sJIA-MAS dominant rheumatologic cause.

adult.trajectory_modulation: Lymphoma-associated HLH dominant; older age worse prognosis.

dermatomyositis.trajectory_modulation: Dermatomyositis is a recognized autoimmune/rheumatic trigger context for secondary HLH/MAS.

supportive_care: Early ICU triage in any HLH/MAS with hypotension, MOF, or rapidly worsening cytopenia/coagulopathy
Aggressive infectious workup: blood cultures, EBV/CMV/HHV6/HIV/hepatitis viruses, leishmania (smear/PCR/serology), TB, atypical pathogens; broad empirical antimicrobials while diagnosis is clarified
Bone marrow biopsy with hemophagocytosis assessment, flow cytometry, and lymphoma staging when adult; LN biopsy if lymphadenopathy
HLH-2004 criteria assessment + HScore + MAS-2016 (sJIA) + MS score (lymphoma-HLH) for diagnostic probability
Quantitative biomarkers serially: ferritin, sIL-2R/sCD25, CXCL9, fibrinogen, triglycerides, ALT/AST, bilirubin, LDH, D-dimer, PT/aPTT, IL-18 if available

NK cell function and perforin/granzyme expression by flow cytometry; SAP/XIAP expression in males with EBV-HLH; genetic panel (PRF1, UNC13D, STX11, STXBP2, RAB27A, XIAP, SH2D1A, LYST) when primary HLH suspected
LP with CSF cell count, protein, opening pressure plus brain MRI if any neurologic feature, including subtle irritability or headache

Aggressive transfusion support: platelets to keep ≥20–50×10⁹/L (higher if bleeding/procedures), cryoprecipitate/fibrinogen concentrate to keep fibrinogen >100–150 mg/dL, FFP for active bleeding/procedures
Avoid prophylactic anticoagulation in active coagulopathy; mechanical DVT prophylaxis preferred until coagulopathy controlled

PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX or alternative) on prolonged steroids/etoposide; antifungal prophylaxis (mold-active in prolonged neutropenia or post-HSCT); HSV/VZV prophylaxis with acyclovir; CMV monitoring with preemptive therapy
HBV screening (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs) before rituximab/JAKi/etoposide; entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis if positive; HCV and HIV screening

Trigger-directed therapy in parallel with HLH-directed therapy: rituximab + steroids/etoposide for EBV-HLH/B-cell lymphoma; lymphoma chemotherapy for T/NK lymphoma; antileishmanial for visceral leishmaniasis; ART in HIV-HLH
Anakinra first-line in MAS from sJIA/AOSD/SLE; consider IV high-dose anakinra (5–10 mg/kg/day) in critically ill MAS
Etoposide (HLH-94/2004) for primary HLH, severe EBV-HLH, lymphoma-associated HLH, refractory secondary HLH; dose-adjust for hepatic/renal function
Emapalumab in refractory/recurrent primary HLH or as bridge to HSCT; serial CXCL9 to monitor pharmacodynamics
Ruxolitinib as salvage in steroid-refractory secondary HLH/MAS, with attention to cytopenia and viral reactivation
Intrathecal methotrexate + hydrocortisone for CNS-HLH per HLH-2004 protocol
Allogeneic HSCT planning early in primary HLH and refractory/relapsed secondary HLH; reduced-intensity conditioning preferred
Cautious calcineurin inhibitor use given PRES risk in active MAS; avoid in uncontrolled hypertension or severe renal impairment
Renal-replacement therapy as needed; hemoperfusion/CRRT with cytokine-removing membranes used in select severe cytokine storms (limited evidence)
Nutritional support including adequate protein and electrolyte management; stress-ulcer prophylaxis on high-dose steroids
Multidisciplinary involvement: hematology, rheumatology, infectious disease, ICU, transplant team, oncology when malignancy suspected
Long-term follow-up: monitor for HLH relapse, secondary AML from etoposide, growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes in pediatrics, ongoing rheumatologic disease control, and post-HSCT chimerism
